workflows.description: Named lifecycle-stage workflows: implement, check, judge, pr-review, pr-respond, pr-update, close-out, define (`lib/config/workflows.ts`'s `BUILTIN_WORKFLOWS`), plus any project-defined name — including the `setup`/`setup-hooks`/`check` baseline names that used to live under their own `verbs:` section, retired: everything lives here now, resolved via `resolveWorkflow(name, projectRoot)`. A step is `{skill}`, `{run}`, `{script}`, `{prompt}`, or a bare string (sugar for `{script: <string>}` — a verb's old shell-command list is spelled identically, just under this key). A `{script}` step may set `process_group: false`: the orchestrator otherwise runs it in its own process group and session, with no controlling terminal, so a `/dev/tty` prompt fails there (`sdlc run` keeps the terminal either way). Every built-in name ships a default step list IN CODE, not here — this map only carries PROJECT overrides. An entry replaces the built-in outright (a bare array, or an object's `steps` key — the two are equivalent), or wraps it with `prepend`/`append` step lists; setting both a full list and `prepend`/`append` on one entry fails validation. A `{run: <name>}` step splices in ANOTHER workflow's already-resolved steps, recursively (cycle-guarded) — not a verb lookup. An entry may also set `profile` or `tool` (exactly one) and `host` with no `steps` at all — the one place a workflow's binding and host live, read by `resolveWorkflow` and dispatched by the orchestrate loop and `sdlc session launch` alike (see `WorkflowEntryObjectSchema`'s own doc). `profile` names a `profiles:` entry; `tool` is a reference such as `codex` or `claude/opus@high`, or a wildcard such as `*/max` (quoted in YAML), which expands through `router.chains.order` or the built-in order. An unattended dispatch (`sdlc orchestrate`, `sdlc run <workflow>`) always launches headless: a profile skips an entry sdlc cannot launch headless, and a `tool` that cannot is rejected before any step runs. `engine` was removed in favour of these two keys. A name absent from this map, and not one of the eight built-ins, resolves to an empty step list. This section is data only: it carries no runner logic, so `sdlc session launch` and a later flowline runner can execute the same resolved list.

items.description: One workflow step: `{skill, args?}`, `{run}`, `{script, read_only?}`, `{prompt}`, or a bare string — sugar for `{script: <string>}`.

skill.description: A skill name (e.g. `task-work`), invoked the way a future `sdlc session launch --skill` will.

args.description: Positional arguments passed through to the skill invocation.

run.description: The name of ANOTHER `workflows:` entry, whose already-resolved steps are spliced in here, recursively (cycle-guarded by a visited-name check) — NOT a literal shell command, and not a verb lookup. `resolveWorkflow` (`lib/config/workflows.ts`) expands every `run:` step before returning, so by resolution time only `skill`/`prompt`/`script` steps remain; each spliced-in leaf is trust-gated exactly as if it had been written inline at the splice site.

script.description: A script to run: usually a project-root-relative path, but a built-in default that needs arguments (e.g. `pr-update`) may carry a literal command line with `{placeholder}` tokens instead. No templating happens in config resolution — a caller substitutes placeholders itself.

read_only.description: Declares that the script writes nothing to the working tree. A scheduled workflow made only of read-only script steps defaults its `output` to `none`; any other step (`skill`, `prompt`, or an unmarked `script`) defaults it to `pr`. Declared, never inferred from the command.

process_group.description: Unset or `true`: the orchestrator runs the step in its own process group and session, so a kill, or a signal sdlc gets, reaches every process the step started. `false` runs it without a group and keeps the terminal. A step in its own session has no controlling terminal, so a prompt on `/dev/tty` fails: a git credential prompt, an ssh passphrase, `pinentry-curses`. A `SIGKILL` sent to the caller's process group (for example `timeout -s KILL`) no longer reaches the step's processes, and a `SIGKILL` of sdlc itself cannot be forwarded, so either leaves the step's tree running. Once the step's `sh` exits, a process it left in the background that still holds the step's output is killed 250 ms later. Redirect its output (`cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 &`) to let it outlive the step. A signal to sdlc does not reach a detached `orchestrate work-run`, which has its own session; stop it with `orchestrate work-stop`. `sdlc run` streams its steps with inherited stdio and keeps the terminal either way.

prompt.description: Literal prompt text handed to the session as-is.

steps.description: Full replacement step list — equivalent to writing the array directly as the whole entry value.
