process_group.description: `true` (default) runs the step in its own process group and session, so a kill, or a signal sdlc gets, reaches every process the step started. Set `false` for a step that must prompt; a kill then reaches only its `sh`. A step in its own session has no controlling terminal, so a prompt on `/dev/tty` fails: a git credential prompt, an ssh passphrase, `pinentry-curses`. A `SIGKILL` sent to the caller's process group (for example `timeout -s KILL`) no longer reaches the step's processes, and a `SIGKILL` of sdlc itself cannot be forwarded, so either leaves the step's tree running. Once the step's `sh` exits, a process it left in the background that still holds the step's output is killed 250 ms later. Redirect its output (`cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 &`) to let it outlive the step. A signal to sdlc does not reach a detached `orchestrate work-run`, which has its own session; stop it with `orchestrate work-stop`.

harness.description: Which agent harnesses `sdlc apply` installs sdlc into. A change here takes effect only after `sdlc apply` re-installs.

targets.description: Agent harnesses to install the sdlc plugin surface for, by exporter name (`sdlc harness export --target` lists them). Absent means the harness applier picks its default.

notify.description: Notification channels and the event catalog — see the `notify` section. This variant omits the cross-field check that an `events.*` channel name exists in `channels`, since a single file may legitimately carry only half of a project's notify config.

channels.description: Named notification channels, each an object discriminated by `type`: `{type: "desktop"}` (no other fields — raises a notification on the machine running the loop); `{type: "ntfy", topic_url}` (POSTs to an ntfy HTTP topic URL); or `{type: "webhook", url, format?}` (POSTs a JSON body to an arbitrary HTTP endpoint — `format` is `slack`, `discord`, or `raw`, default `raw`). Each name is referenced by one or more `events.*` lists below; a channel not referenced by any event is valid but inert.

oneOf.description: Raise a desktop notification on the machine running the loop (`osascript` on macOS, `notify-send` on Linux; degrades to a stderr log elsewhere).

topic_url.description: Full ntfy topic URL to POST each notification to.

oneOf.description: Push notifications through an ntfy HTTP topic.

url.description: Webhook URL to POST each notification to. A secret: keep it in `sdlc.local.yaml`.

format.description: Request body shape: `slack` (`{text: message}`), `discord` (`{content: message}`), or `raw` (`{event, message, ...payload}`, the default) — see `lib/services/notify/webhook.ts#notifyWebhook`.

oneOf.description: POST a JSON body to an arbitrary HTTP endpoint — a Slack or Discord incoming webhook, or any other listener.

events.description: Exactly the 15 canonical event names, each an ordered list of channel names (from `channels` above) to fire when that event happens. An event key that is absent, or set to `[]`, is a silent no-op — no channel call, no error. An unknown event key fails validation.

pr.needs_response.description: A PR classified NEEDS-RESPONSE has exhausted `orchestrator.review.max_rounds` review/respond round-trips (`ticks/_pr_action.ts`). Fires on every orchestrator tick thereafter for as long as the PR stays stuck in that state — there is no dedup or one-shot suppression, so a configured channel repeats this notification, not just once.

pr.ci_failed.description: A PR classified CI-FAILED has exhausted `orchestrator.review.max_rounds` review/respond round-trips (`ticks/_pr_action.ts`). Fires on every orchestrator tick thereafter for as long as the PR stays stuck in that state — there is no dedup or one-shot suppression, so a configured channel repeats this notification, not just once.

task.parked.description: A task's dispatch is stood down, whether by a blocking hook (`sdlc hooks run` consumes a park marker for the task's branch) or by the `work` tick's own step-failure handling when a dispatched workflow step fails outright (`ticks/work.ts`). The payload carries a `focus` field, the `sdlc session focus …` command for the task.

stage.ceiling_reached.description: A chain-labeled issue is already at its `sdlc:auto/<x>` autonomy ceiling (the `issues` tick).

phase.ready_for_review.description: A phase reached ready-for-review. No detector wired yet.

lease.expired.description: A lease expired (`sdlc lease reconcile`'s `expired-task-leases` detector). `notifyExpiredLeaseAnomalies` (`reconcile.ts`) collapses every anomaly found in ONE reconcile run into a single notify, but that dedup does not persist across runs: the same still-expired lease fires again on every subsequent `sdlc lease reconcile` run for as long as it stays expired — there is no cross-run dedup or one-shot suppression, the same unbounded-repeat shape as `pr.needs_response`/`pr.ci_failed` above.

session.ended.description: An agent session ended: fires whenever a headless session record is finalized. The orchestrate step-runner launching a headless skill/prompt step for a workflow tick is the common case in practice; a direct `sdlc session launch --headless` invocation is the other.

session.waiting.description: An interactive Claude session entered `waiting_for_input` (a permission or elicitation prompt, or an `AskUserQuestion`): fires once per entry from the hook reporter (`sdlc session hook`), not on each repeated hook while it stays waiting. The payload carries a `focus` field, the `sdlc session focus …` command that brings the session forward.

session.done.description: An agent declared its session done with `sdlc session done` (`outcome` is `ok` or `failed`). The session stays open for a next prompt; this is not `session.ended`. The payload carries a `focus` field, the `sdlc session focus …` command that brings the session forward.

hook.blocked.description: An `on_fail: block` hook step failed (`sdlc hooks run`).

orchestrator.dead_stop.description: The orchestrate loop stopped dead. No detector wired yet.

usage.budget_exceeded.description: A usage.budget ceiling (tokens or cost_usd) was exceeded within its rolling window AND the work tick actually had a ready candidate it would otherwise have dispatched this tick (ticks/work.ts) — never fires while already `orchestrate pause`d (that gate is the more informative status) or when there was nothing ready to dispatch anyway. Still repeats every tick that meets both conditions for as long as usage stays over the ceiling — no one-shot-per-crossing suppression, but scoped to ticks where the event's claim ("dispatch was suppressed") is actually true.

orchestrator.base_red.description: The `work` tick found the tip of `origin/<target>` failing a `orchestrator.base_health.commands` command and stopped dispatching new work (`services/orchestrator/base-health.ts`). Fires once per (sha, command), not once per tick, and not while the `work` loop is paused or on a dry run. Runs already going continue.

orchestrator.base_unverified.description: The base-health check could not answer for a sha: a spawn error, a timeout, or a failed fetch, worktree reset or install. Distinct from `orchestrator.base_red`: no command failed, so nothing is cached red; the check is retried after `orchestrator.base_health.infra_retry_seconds` and the `work` tick dispatches nothing until it has a verdict. Fires once per sha, not once per retry, and not while paused or on a dry run.

orchestrator.base_green.description: The base turned green after a red one was announced (a new sha passed): the `work` tick dispatches again. Fires once per recovery, and not while paused or on a dry run.

mcp.description: Which ops the `sdlc mcp` stdio server exposes as tools. Safe default: only ops marked `mutating: false` are exposed; `allow` opts specific mutating ops in, `deny` excludes specific ops. `sdlc apply` registers the server with each harness, so a change to the registration takes effect only after it runs.

allow.description: Additional op paths (space-joined, e.g. "task create") to expose as MCP tools even though they are not marked mutating: false. Opt-in for mutating ops.

deny.description: Op paths (space-joined) to exclude from the MCP tool set even if they would otherwise qualify (e.g. a read-only op you don't want exposed).

knowledge.description: Reserved for knowledge-base settings. No field is defined yet.

issues.description: Reserved for issue-tracker sync and the issues loop (sdlc 1.0 Phase 7). No field is defined yet.

usage.description: Token/cost usage reporting, the budget gate and the rate-limit cooldown cap. `budget` sets a rolling-window token/cost ceiling that pauses the work tick's dispatch and fires `usage.budget_exceeded` when exceeded. Absent, or present with `budget` absent (or both `budget.tokens`/`budget.cost_usd` unset), means no cap — inert, matching `notify.channels`' 'valid but inert' precedent.

budget.description: Token/cost ceiling that pauses the orchestrator work tick's dispatch and fires usage.budget_exceeded when exceeded. Absent, or present with both `tokens`/`cost_usd` unset, means no cap — inert, matching notify.channels' 'valid but inert' precedent.

window_hours.description: Rolling lookback window (hours, ending now) that budget totals are summed over.

tokens.description: Total token ceiling, compared against a BILLABLE per-window sum: UsageRow.inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheWriteTokens, nulls counting as 0 — deliberately EXCLUDING cacheReadTokens (see lib/services/usage/record.ts#sumBillableTokens). Cache reads dominate raw usage and are far cheaper than fresh input, so a ceiling compared against the cache-inclusive ledger total (UsageRow.totalTokens) would trip within a single session. Unset: no token ceiling.

cost_usd.description: Total USD cost ceiling (sum of UsageRow.costUsd, nulls counting as 0) across rows inside the window. Only a headless Claude run ever populates a non-null costUsd (claude -p --output-format json's own total_cost_usd) — every interactive row and every codex row (headless or interactive) is always costUsd: null, since codex reports no dollar figure and there is no local price table. This ceiling therefore only ever caps headless-Claude spend, not total spend. Unset: no cost ceiling.

cooldown_max_hours.description: The longest a rate-limit cooldown (`.sdlc/cooldowns.json`) keeps a tool or model out of routing, in hours. A reset time the tool reports further out, or a stale entry further out, counts only this long; the tool is then tried again and re-cooled if still limited. The writer clamps to it and every reader applies it. Unset: 24.

schedules.description: Named schedules: each runs a workflow on a five-field cron expression, with a per-run time limit. Entries merge by `name` across `sdlc.yaml` and `sdlc.local.yaml`. A bad cron expression or time zone, an unknown workflow, a duplicate name or a missing `limits.minutes` refuses to load. Runs only while the orchestrator loop is on.

name.description: Unique name of the schedule. The merge key across `sdlc.yaml` and `sdlc.local.yaml`: a local entry with an existing name replaces the project entry whole.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Fields take `*`, lists, ranges, steps and month/weekday names.

tz.description: IANA time zone the cron expression is read in (for example `Europe/Berlin`). Unset: the machine zone.

run.description: Name of the workflow to run: an entry in `workflows:` or a built-in workflow.

on_late.description: What to do when a slot was missed (the orchestrator loop was off): `run` it once now, or `skip` it and wait for the next slot. Unset: `due()` applies its half-interval rule.

output.description: Where a run leaves its changes: `none` (nothing is kept), `pr` (open a pull request) or `branch` (push a branch). `main` is never accepted: output never lands on the default branch. Unset: `pr` when the workflow has a `skill` or `prompt` step or a `script` step not marked `read_only`, else `none`.

minutes.description: Per-run time limit in minutes, covering every step of the workflow, agent or script. Required: an unattended run always has a ceiling. An entry never overlaps itself, so there is no per-entry concurrency cap.

limits.description: Guardrails for each run of this schedule.

runner.description: Per-machine choice to keep the orchestrator running without a terminal: a launchd agent (macOS) or systemd user unit (Linux) that runs `sdlc orchestrate run` with restart on failure. Lives in `sdlc.local.yaml` only; unset installs nothing, and schedules then run only while `sdlc orchestrate run` is up. `sdlc apply` installs and removes the unit; `sdlc project doctor` flags a missing unit or one whose project moved.

kind.description: Which OS service manager runs `sdlc orchestrate run` for this project: `launchd` (macOS user agent), `systemd` (Linux user unit) or `none` (no runner; removes one `sdlc apply` installed earlier). A kind that does not match this machine is reported and changes nothing.

parent.description: Root of this project's parent project, when it has one. Recorded with the project in the machine's runner list; the runner itself does not use it.
